policy.summary: A bounded dynamic hook-delta fee rises with positive observed quote-per-base tick velocity and decays toward the creator's minimum as the signal ages.
policy.formula: For minimum m, maximum M, sensitivity G, positive observed tick change D and elapsed signal age E: ratePips = min(M, m + floor(G * D / E)). Warm-up, D <= 0, E == 0 or G == 0 uses m; equal bounds use their common rate. feeRaw = floor(feeBearingAmountRaw * ratePips / 1000000).

hookFeePips.description: Maximum trading rate M in fee pips; the upward-velocity uplift saturates at this cap.

minimumHookFeePips.description: Minimum trading rate m in fee pips, independent of the maximum; used during warm-up, flat or falling signals and after idle decay reaches the floor.

feeSensitivityPipsSecondsPerTick.description: Sensitivity G in fee-pips times seconds per tick. Larger values amplify positive observed velocity; zero disables the uplift and fixes the rate at the minimum.

oracle.description: Composes PoolBoundTruncatedOracleV2 with initial capacity two. Fewer than two genuine observations or a zero-length interval yields no velocity signal. D is current truncated tick minus the previously held tick, normalized to quote per base; E is time since the previous observation, including idle age. The pre-swap rate freezes before the swap's oracle checkpoint.

behavior.warmup: Charges the creator's minimum until two genuine observations and a positive elapsed interval are available.
behavior.flatOrFalling: A nonpositive observed truncated tick change charges the minimum. A flat raw spot price can still leave a positive lagging truncated signal.
behavior.idle: For an unchanged positive sampled signal, increasing elapsed age reduces uplift with integer cap/floor plateaus. New observations and clamp catch-up can prevent monotonic decay across consecutive trades.
behavior.zeroSensitivity: Charges the minimum independently of the observed movement.
behavior.zeroMaximum: Maximum zero requires minimum zero and produces zero trading fees.

risks: Truncated sampling, per-block clamping and pre-swap rate freezing introduce lag; oracle history is not a manipulation-resistance guarantee.
Thin liquidity, adversarial price paths and repeated trading can affect the sampled signal; the oracle is not an external fair-value feed.
High sensitivity can reach the cap quickly, and positive rates can still round to zero fees on small raw amounts.
External LPs receive no native swap-fee allocation from this zero-LP-fee policy; donations or a separately approved rewards allocation would be distinct mechanisms.
A nonzero PoolManager protocol fee makes the inherited hook reject swaps; previews are not guaranteed future execution quotes.
These declared descriptions are not artifact qualification, author consent, an audit or production registry admission.
